modeSemantics.normal: Target contract classification for reliable business behavior; not a current runtime selector.
modeSemantics.practice: Target contract classification for automation exercises; not a current runtime selector.
modeSemantics.defect-lab: Target contract classification only; no defect-lab scenario is published in this catalog.

storageModes.memory: Legacy Express memory storage exposed through /api; forced by SHOPLAB_STORAGE=legacy or used when DATABASE_URL is absent.
storageModes.postgres: PostgreSQL storage exposed through /api/v2 when DATABASE_URL is configured and SHOPLAB_STORAGE is not legacy.

fixtureSemantics.details: No fixture-version API or immutable published fixture bundle exists. fixtureVersion is null on every scenario rather than inventing a version. Current prerequisites name the existing seed or disposable-account mechanism.

resetSemantics.legacy-global: Playwright global setup calls POST /api/reset once before the legacy reference run. This is global and destructive to disposable memory state, not a run-scoped reset.
resetSemantics.disposable-postgres-cleanup: The database smoke script removes its own disposable account and related records. This is cleanup for that script, not a general scenario-reset API.
resetSemantics.unavailable: No scenario-scoped or test-run-scoped reset endpoint is implemented.

scenarios.title: Standard customer signs in and restores an authenticated session
prerequisites: Run against a disposable legacy-memory environment with the current seed.
Use the standard_user fixture identifier and PASSWORD from tests/support/test-data.ts; do not copy credentials into an external manifest.
Start with a signed-out browser context.

steps.action: Open /login, fill the username and password, and submit.
Open the signed-in user menu after navigation to /shop.
For the separate storage assertion, inspect localStorage after UI login.

observableResults: The browser reaches /shop.
A toast containing Welcome back is visible.
The signed-in identity is standard_user.
The separate session test observes a UUID-shaped token under shoplab.token.
scenarios.timeoutPolicy: Existing Playwright defaults: 30000 ms test timeout and 7000 ms assertion timeout.

reset.details: The reference suite resets global memory state once in global setup; there is no per-scenario reset.

scenarios.cleanup: Close the browser context. Seeded users remain until the next legacy global reset.
knownLimitations: This scenario describes the legacy seeded login, not PostgreSQL authenticator MFA.
Session persistence is evidenced by the existing token test; this is not a cross-browser or long-duration expiry certification.

scenarios.title: Legacy email OTP challenge uses the matching test-inbox message
prerequisites: Run against legacy memory storage with the mfa_user seed and test mailbox available.
Start signed out and use the PASSWORD fixture from tests/support/test-data.ts.

steps.action: Sign in as mfa_user and capture the login response mfaToken.
Read the test mailbox and select the message whose ref equals this login response's mfaToken.
Type the six-digit code into the first auto-advancing digit input and submit.

observableResults: Password login navigates to /login/verify.
data-testid=otp-sent-to displays m***@shoplab.test.
A matching mailbox message supplies the current code even if other mailbox entries exist.
Successful verification reaches /shop and data-testid=user-name is Mfa User.
scenarios.timeoutPolicy: Existing Playwright defaults: 30000 ms test timeout and 7000 ms assertion timeout.

reset.details: Only the legacy global reset is available; mailbox and challenge state are not run-scoped.

scenarios.cleanup: Close the browser context. Mailbox and memory fixtures remain until global reset.
knownLimitations: This is legacy email OTP, not PostgreSQL authenticator TOTP or backup-code MFA.
The test mailbox is a development/test surface and must not be treated as a production email integration.

scenarios.title: PostgreSQL authenticator enrollment, backup-code sign-in, and disablement
prerequisites: Use an authorized disposable PostgreSQL development environment and a newly registered smoke account.
Build the current TypeScript backend before running the existing database smoke script.
Generate TOTP values at runtime from the enrollment secret with the pinned otplib dependency.
Keep generated secrets, passwords, tokens, and backup codes out of the catalog and external reports.

steps.action: Open security settings, enter the disposable account's current password, and begin enrollment.
Read the enrollment secret, generate the current TOTP, submit it, and capture the eight one-use backup codes.
Sign out, authenticate with the disposable username and password, then use one backup code at the challenge.
Return to security settings and disable MFA with the current password and a different backup code.

observableResults: Enrollment returns a secret and exactly eight backup codes.
Backup-code verification reaches /shop.
After disablement, data-testid=mfa-status is Not enabled.
The smoke flow consumes different backup codes for sign-in and disablement.
scenarios.timeoutPolicy: Use the database smoke script's waits and overall test timeout; do not shorten security-state waits without rerunning the source scenario.

reset.details: No run-scoped reset exists. The smoke script instead deletes its disposable account and related records.

scenarios.cleanup: Use the existing smoke-v2-storefront.cjs cleanupUser path for its own disposable account; never substitute a global database reset.
knownLimitations: The current smoke proves enrollment, backup-code sign-in, and disablement; it is not a complete replay-rejection or authenticator-interoperability matrix.
The scenario uses variables from a disposable runtime account and must never contain hard-coded database IDs, generated secrets, or credentials.

scenarios.title: Customer is denied admin navigation and admin API access
prerequisites: Run against legacy memory storage.
Authenticate as a freshly registered non-admin customer through the existing user fixture.

steps.action: Open /admin as the customer and inspect the main navigation.
With the same customer API context, request the tested admin endpoints, including a write attempt.

observableResults: data-testid=access-denied contains Access denied.
The Admin link in Main navigation is hidden.
Every tested admin API request returns HTTP 403.
scenarios.timeoutPolicy: Existing Playwright defaults: 30000 ms test timeout and 7000 ms assertion timeout.

reset.details: The reference run uses the global memory reset, not an authorization-specific reset.

scenarios.cleanup: Close customer API and browser contexts; no admin records should be created.
knownLimitations: The endpoint list is the current reference set, not a proof that every possible future admin route is covered.
Hiding navigation is supporting UI evidence; HTTP 403 is the authorization assertion.

scenarios.title: Price range and in-stock filters update the URL and visible products
prerequisites: Run as a guest against the current legacy product seed.
Use products returned by the current catalog rather than row position as product identity.

steps.action: Open /shop and wait for the product grid to finish loading.
Set minimum price to 20 and maximum price to 50, then apply the price filter.
Check In stock only and wait for the grid again.
Read every displayed product price and search the visible cards for Out of stock.

observableResults: The URL contains minPrice=20, maxPrice=50, and inStock=true.
Every displayed price is between 20 and 50 inclusive.
No visible product card contains Out of stock.
scenarios.timeoutPolicy: Existing Playwright defaults: 30000 ms test timeout and 7000 ms assertion timeout; wait for aria-busy=false after each filter.

reset.details: Filtering is read-only; the suite-level memory reset restores the seed before a run.

scenarios.cleanup: Clear filters or close the guest browser context; no persistent user records are created.
knownLimitations: This exact filter assertion is sourced from the legacy reference test, not the PostgreSQL smoke.
The scenario verifies visible results and URL state, not the database query plan or all pagination combinations.

scenarios.title: Customer searches, checks out, and opens the persisted order detail
prerequisites: Use a signed-in disposable customer and an authorized disposable environment.
Resolve Robot Building Kit by search and visible product name; never hard-code a PostgreSQL product ID.
For PostgreSQL, use the current seeded catalog and the existing database smoke script with its own newly registered account.
Use only the published test card data from tests/support/test-data.ts; no real payment details.

steps.action: Search for robot and open the exact Robot Building Kit product by its visible product-name link.
Increase quantity from one to two and add the product to the cart.
Open Cart, record the order-summary total, and proceed to checkout.
Complete Address, Delivery, Payment, and Review using the existing checkout fixtures.
Verify the review, accept the terms, place the order, and retain the generated order ID.
selectors: role=checkbox name=/I agree to the terms of sale/

steps.action: Open View order and compare its identity, status, and total with confirmation.

observableResults: The cart badge is 2 after adding quantity two.
The review shows card last4 4242, Robot Building Kit × 2, and the same total recorded in the cart.
Confirmation displays Thank you for your order!, a generated order ID, and the unchanged total.
The cart badge returns to 0.
Order detail shows the generated order ID, Placed, and the unchanged total.
The PostgreSQL smoke additionally covers SAVE10, express shipping, invoice download, and cancellation with a generated order ID.
scenarios.timeoutPolicy: Legacy uses Playwright defaults. The PostgreSQL smoke allows 25000 ms for navigation to checkout completion.

reset.details: Memory has only the global suite reset. PostgreSQL has no run-scoped reset; the smoke cleans up only its disposable account and related records.

scenarios.cleanup: For memory, close the context and use the next authorized global reset. For PostgreSQL, let the existing smoke cleanup cancel and remove its own orders and account; do not reset shared data.
knownLimitations: The exact Robot Building Kit, total-equality, and View order assertions are from the legacy test; the PostgreSQL smoke covers the same business flow but is not an identical step-for-step trace.

This scenario alone does not prove stored-total integrity, stock reduction, duplicate-request idempotency, or cancellation stock restoration; those require separate API/database invariants before claiming full contract acceptance.
A success toast or confirmation page alone is not sufficient evidence; retain the generated order ID and inspect order detail.

scenarios.title: Customer confirms or aborts cancellation from order detail
prerequisites: Authenticate as a disposable customer and create an order owned by that customer.
Resolve orderId at runtime from the created order or confirmation page; never hard-code a PostgreSQL ID.
The order must still be in a cancellable state.

steps.action: Open the generated order detail and select Cancel order.
In the confirmation dialog named Cancel {orderId}?, choose Keep order.
Reopen cancellation and choose Yes, cancel order.

observableResults: Keep order leaves status Placed.
Confirmed cancellation changes status to Cancelled.
The Cancelled timeline step has data-done=true.
The Cancel order button is hidden after cancellation.
The PostgreSQL smoke confirms cancellation through data-testid=cancel-order, data-testid=confirm-ok, and data-testid=order-status.
scenarios.timeoutPolicy: Existing Playwright defaults; wait for the server-backed order status rather than assuming the click is sufficient.

reset.details: No scenario-scoped reset exists. The memory suite resets globally; PostgreSQL smoke removes its own disposable records.

scenarios.cleanup: Retain the cancelled order for assertions, then use only the owning test's existing cleanup path.
knownLimitations: The Keep order dialog branch is asserted in the legacy test; the PostgreSQL smoke confirms the cancellation branch.
Stock restoration and financial side effects are not asserted by this UI scenario and must not be inferred from status text alone.

scenarios.title: Native alert, confirm, and prompt produce observable lab results
prerequisites: Open /lab in a guest browser context.
Register one-shot dialog handlers before clicking each triggering button.

steps.action: Within the dialogs lab card, accept the alert and assert its type and message.
Dismiss the confirm dialog.
Accept the prompt with Rupesh and verify its default value was Tester.

observableResults: The alert message is Hello from VORTEX! and the result is Alert dismissed.
Dismissing confirm produces Confirmed: Cancel.
Accepting the prompt produces Hello, Rupesh!.
scenarios.timeoutPolicy: Existing Playwright defaults: 30000 ms test timeout and 7000 ms assertion timeout.

reset.details: The lab is client-side practice state; no scenario-scoped reset endpoint exists. Reloading resets the card for a fresh context.

scenarios.cleanup: Close the browser context; no database record is required.
knownLimitations: Browser automation must handle native dialogs through tool events, not DOM locators.
This is target Practice classification, not evidence of an implemented Practice mode selector.

scenarios.title: Nested frames preserve independent interaction contexts
prerequisites: Open /lab in a guest browser context.
Use frame locators rooted at the published outer-frame and inner-frame test IDs.

steps.action: Inside the outer frame, click the button initially named Clicked 0 times.
From the outer frame, enter the nested inner frame, fill Your name with Rupesh, and select Greet.

observableResults: The outer frame counter becomes Clicked 1 time.
The inner frame greeting becomes Hello, Rupesh!.
scenarios.timeoutPolicy: Existing Playwright defaults: 30000 ms test timeout and 7000 ms assertion timeout.

reset.details: No frame-specific reset API exists; use a fresh page or reload /lab.

scenarios.cleanup: Close the browser context; no persistent business records are created.
knownLimitations: A page-level locator is not a substitute for the correct frame context.
The scenario does not claim cross-origin iframe support beyond the current lab pages.

scenarios.title: Open shadow roots are selectable and closed internals stay behind the public API
prerequisites: Open /lab in a guest browser context and scope locators to data-testid=lab-shadow.
Use an automation tool with open-shadow-root locator support.
Do not rely on closed-root internals; use only the component's documented public reveal method.

steps.action: Select the 4 stars button inside the open shadow component.
Inspect the nested open shadow chip and its slotted light-DOM text.
Assert that the closed-root Reveal secret button is not locator-visible, then call reveal() on closed-shadow-host.

observableResults: The rating text is You rated 4/5 and shadow-host has value=4.
The nested chip has part=chip and lab-chip contains shadow-in-shadow.
No Reveal secret button is selectable through the closed root.
Calling the public reveal() method sets revealed=true on closed-shadow-host.
scenarios.timeoutPolicy: Existing Playwright defaults: 30000 ms test timeout and 7000 ms assertion timeout.

reset.details: No shadow-component reset endpoint exists; use a fresh page or reload /lab.

scenarios.cleanup: Close the browser context; no persistent business records are created.
knownLimitations: Closed-root internals are deliberately not promised to be selectable.
Calling reveal() is component API interaction, not general closed-shadow-root piercing.
Open-root locator behavior is tool-specific; another recorder must demonstrate equivalent behavior before claiming compatibility.
